title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR 2 — peccandi verbum sometimes = consequent reatus (antecedent for consequent)
pass_a_gloss: GAR's second point: Scripture sometimes lets the verb of sinning stand for the guilt that follows from sin. That is the familiar trope of putting the antecedent for the consequent—so 'sinning' names the reatus rather than the act alone.
pass_b_english: GAR. 2. Nor is it unknown in Scripture that the word of sinning sometimes signifies the guilt consequent from sin, according to that manner of speaking by which the antecedent is put for the consequent.
source_text: GAR. 2. Neque ignotum est in Scriptura peccandi verbum aliquando significare reatum ex peccato consequentem, secundum illam loquendi rationem qua ponitur antecedens pro consequente.

choices.choice: Scripture sometimes uses 'sin' for consequent reatus (antecedent→consequent)
